entities.summary: Linda Lee Fagan is a retired American admiral who served as the 27th commandant of the United States Coast Guard from June 2022 to January 2025. Previously, she was the 32nd vice commandant of the Coast Guard under Commandant Karl L. Schultz from 2021 to 2022. Before that, she was the commander of the Coast Guard Pacific Area with prior terms as Coast Guard Deputy for Operations, Policy, and Capabilities; commander, First Coast Guard District; and commander, Coast Guard Sector New York. Fagan is also the Coast Guard's first Gold Ancient Trident, the officer with the longest service record in the marine safety field.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first female Gold Ancient Trident with a record-breaking 47 years of service, Linda Fagan's leadership has had significant regional impact on maritime safety and security in North America. Her tenure as Coast Guard commandant has set a precedent for future generations of women in senior leadership positions.
